subject.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue

question: Should OpenClaw's command-queue starvation guard be the PR's foreground-preserving one-tier aging policy, or should aged background work eventually overtake fresh foreground work after the threshold?
rationale: Both policies are plausible and affect user-visible session ordering under contention; source review can catch mismatches, but only maintainers can choose the intended fairness contract.

options.title: Accept One-Tier Aging
options.body: Land this PR after aligning the STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS comment and any public docs to the foreground-preserving contract, then track stronger fairness separately.

options.title: Require Strong Aging
options.body: Change the implementation and tests so aged background work can overtake fresh foreground after the threshold, matching the original all-priority starvation proposal.

options.title: Defer To Broader Fairness
options.body: Pause this PR and resolve the queue-reserve or broader scheduler fairness work first if maintainers want capacity reservation or cross-agent scheduling rather than dequeue aging.

recommendation.title: Accept One-Tier Aging
recommendation.body: Land this PR after aligning the STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS comment and any public docs to the foreground-preserving contract, then track stronger fairness separately.

likelyOwner.reason: They have adjacent command-queue history and already closed the competing #80199 in favor of #75299 as the focused policy vehicle.
